prediction_ref.short_label: Consumer-GPU coding agents displace cloud-only APIs for 30% of devs

validation_rows.evidence_summary: [REVIVED] Layer-1 keyword and Layer-2 semantic match against the dormant snapshot's signals (consumer-GPU coding agent, open-weight coding model, SWE-bench Verified, cheaper than cloud API, agentic coding). Today Moonshot released Kimi K2.7-Code, an open-weight coding-specialized model on Hugging Face under a Modified MIT license, a 1-trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts design (about 32B active across 384 experts, 256K context) tuned for long-horizon agentic software engineering and priced at $0.95/$4.00 per million tokens. An openly downloadable, low-cost coding model aimed at agentic software work is the kind of artifact the dormant thesis says erodes cloud-only coding APIs in favor of self-hosted alternatives. But the divergence from the marker is sharp: K2.7-Code is a trillion-parameter MoE rather than the consumer-GPU-runnable dense model the prediction names, today's coverage centers on benchmark credibility rather than local on-device deployment, and no developer-adoption figure is reported. So this is a weak revival of the open-weight-coding-displacement direction, not a match to the consumer-hardware or 30%-of-devs specification.
